content.title: About
content.content: Pinto beans and rice is a popular fast‑food dish consisting of boiled pinto beans mixed with fluffy white rice. It is usually served hot, sometimes topped with spices, sauce, or cheese.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pinto beans originated in Mexico and are among the most nutritious legumes.
The bean‑and‑rice combination provides a complete set of essential amino acids, making it a full‑protein meal.
In the United States the dish is often offered at chain fast‑food restaurants as an inexpensive lunch option.
Pinto beans are rich in antioxidants, especially polyphenols, which give them their characteristic reddish hue.
Traditionally the rice is steamed to keep it light and separate from the beans.

items.title: Rich source of plant protein
items.content: Pinto beans contain about 21 g of protein per 100 g, and rice adds complementary amino acids, enhancing protein quality.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports healthy digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Provides complex carbohydrates
items.content: Rice supplies slowly digestible carbs that help maintain steady energy levels.

items.title: Contains iron and magnesium
items.content: These minerals are important for blood formation and muscle function.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: The dish fits well into low‑fat diets when not paired with heavy sauces.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce mineral absorption; soaking beans before cooking lowers its level.

items.title: High glycemic index of rice
items.content: People monitoring blood sugar may prefer whole‑grain or brown rice instead of white rice.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, often in a disposable container. It can be topped with salsa, guacamole, shredded cheese, or fresh vegetables for added flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. It freezes well for up to 2 months. Reheat to at least 75 °C before eating.
